questions.question_text: Written in the form $(a+b)^2$ with the terms in the order shown, identify $a$ and $b$ for $(6x-5y)^2$.

options.why: Read $b$ off without its sign; the subtraction must be carried into $b$.
Kept only the coefficients and dropped the variables from each term.
Squared each term first; $a$ and $b$ are the terms themselves, before squaring.
Squared each term separately and left out the middle term $2ab=8x$.
Used $ab=4x$ for the middle term instead of doubling it to $2ab=8x$.
Doubled the $4$ instead of squaring it for the last term.
Kept the minus on the last term; $(-11)^2$ is positive $121$.
Used $b=11$ instead of $b=-11$, so the middle term came out positive.
Treated the repeated bracket as a difference of two squares, dropping the middle term.
Squared the $x$ but not the coefficient, writing $(3x)^2$ as $3x^2$.
Used $ab=6x$ for the middle term instead of doubling it to $2ab=12x$.
Squared each term separately and left out the middle term altogether.
Added the squares instead of subtracting; the identity gives $a^2-b^2$.
Wrote the squares the wrong way round; $a$ is the first term $y$, not $9$.
Expanded as if both brackets were $(y-9)$, keeping a middle term that actually cancels.
Squared the variables but not the coefficients $4$ and $3$.
Added the two squares instead of subtracting the second.
Kept a middle term of $-24mn$; the two middle products cancel each other.
Squared the $k$ but not the coefficient, writing $(3k)^2$ as $3k^2$.
Took $a=3k$ and $b=10$; here the first term of each bracket is $10$.
Added the squares instead of subtracting the square of the second term.
Multiplied the indices when squaring, giving $x^3 \times x^3 = x^9$ instead of $x^6$.
Squared the $x^3$ but left the coefficient $2$ unsquared.
Added the two squares instead of subtracting the second.
Used $b=5t$ instead of $b=-5t$, so the middle term came out positive.
Kept the minus when squaring $-5t$; $(-5t)^2$ is positive $25t^2$.
Used $ab=-30t$ for the middle term instead of doubling it to $2ab=-60t$.
